newsitem.title: USA: Bosnian president says top Serbs must be prosecuted.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian president says top Serbs must be prosecuted.

text.p: Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic said on Monday that peace cannot be ensured in Bosnia until top former Serb leaders are prosecuted for war crimes.

Izetbegovic told reporters that former Bosnia Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and his army commander Gen. Ratko Mladic maintain influence and must be prosecuted on war crime charges by a U.N. criminal tribunal for former Yugoslavia at The Hague.
"Peace cannot be ensured until Karadzic and Mladic would be sent to the tribunal," Izetbegovic said. He was meeting with U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Monday.

When asked if the United States should do more to ensure prosecution of war criminals, he said "I insisted on that. I (said) to the secretary of defence that this is essential and maybe he can answer better than me to this question."
Cohen made no comment at a brief photo session with Izetbegovic but has said before that allies are considering creation of a special police force to apprehend indicted war criminals.
Karadzic and Mladic were indicted by the tribunal and charged with genocide for the slaughter of up to 6,000 Moslems civilians in Srebrenica when Serbs controlled the area.
